faqGeneral.a: A child-centered approach where children learn by doing. They choose hands-on activities and work at their own pace in a carefully prepared classroom.

faqGeneral.q: What ages do you care for?
faqGeneral.a: Children from 6 weeks to 8 years: infants, toddlers, preschool, Pre-K, private Kindergarten and Summer Bridge.
We are open 6:30am to 6pm, Monday to Friday, 12 months a year, except for announced holidays.
Eagan Montessori Academy South is at 1970 Rahncliff Court, Eagan. Amazing Beginnings Montessori is at 3105 65th St. East, Inver Grove Heights.
We are NAEYC accredited and have a four-star rating from Parent Aware, Minnesota’s top preschool rating.

faqGeneral.q: Do you serve meals and snacks?
faqGeneral.a: Yes. Hot lunches are catered by CKC Good Food, and we serve snacks every day. You may also send your own lunch.

faqGeneral.q: How do you keep children safe?
faqGeneral.a: The main entrance has a coded entry system, and all staff are trained in CPR and First Aid.

faqEnrollment.q: How do I sign up my child?
faqEnrollment.a: Call us or send a message. We will set up a tour and walk you through the next steps.
Call us with your start date. We then meet for a short intake interview and you fill out the enrollment form.
Tuition depends on age group and schedule. Full-time and part-time options are available. Contact us for details.
Some programs may have a waitlist. We encourage early applications and will keep you updated.
Yes, we give enrollment priority to siblings.

faqInfant.q: How are the infant rooms organized?
faqInfant.a: Babies are grouped by stage: a room for the youngest (6 weeks to crawling), a crawling room, and a room that prepares for toddler class.
Infants follow their own individual sleep schedules.

faqInfant.q: How will I know how my baby’s day went?
faqInfant.a: You get a daily journal with photos and notes, plus a monthly newsletter.
Yes. Both full-time and part-time infant care are available.

infant.lead: Caring, Montessori-inspired care for babies from 6 weeks old.
infant.description: Montessori infant childcare from 6 weeks in Eagan and Inver Grove Heights. 1:4 ratio, full-time and part-time care.
infant.body:
A calm, safe start

Our infant rooms give babies a safe, interesting space to rest, explore and grow, with caring adults who watch and follow each child’s needs.

Full-time and part-time infant care are available at both schools.

Classrooms grouped by stage

  • Our tiniest classroom: from 6 weeks until babies start to crawl, with tummy time and lots of face-to-face play.
  • Crawling classroom: textured floors, toys and climbing equipment for busy movers.
  • Getting ready for toddlers: small tables and chairs, cot sleeping and eating on their own.

toddler.lead: A language-rich room that builds independence, kindness and friendships.
toddler.description: Montessori toddler program for 16 to 33 months in Eagan and Inver Grove Heights.
toddler.body:
Growing independence

Our toddler rooms help children become more independent, kind and helpful through play, joyful experiences and simple investigations.

Teachers use real words instead of baby talk, so children build a big vocabulary. Books, music and hands-on materials are always within reach.

Two toddler rooms

  • Toddler 1 (about 16 to 24 months): building on skills from the infant rooms, with lots of movement and language.
  • Toddler 2 (up to 33 months): more independence, self-regulation and social skills.

preschool.lead: A prepared Montessori classroom where children learn to do things for themselves.
preschool.description: Montessori preschool for 33 months to 4½ years in Eagan and Inver Grove Heights.
preschool.body:
A prepared Montessori classroom

Everything in the classroom has a place. Children choose their work, use it with care and put it back on the shelf. Teachers work with each child alone and in small groups.

Our preschool rooms support each child’s social, physical and emotional growth, and build independence, grace and courtesy.

Areas of learning

  • Practical Life and Sensorial activities
  • Language, Math and Science
  • Geography, Art and Music
  • Yoga and the S.M.A.R.T. readiness program

prek.lead: Year-round Pre-K and private Kindergarten with a strong Montessori foundation.
prek.description: Montessori Pre-K and year-round private Kindergarten in Eagan and Inver Grove Heights.
prek.body:
Private Kindergarten, all year round

In Pre-K and Kindergarten, children bring their earliest lessons together. Letters are learned by their sounds (phonics), which leads naturally to reading.

Our graduates are well prepared for kindergarten screenings and enrichment programs in District 196 and nearby schools.

What children learn

  • Language arts: reading, writing, spelling and handwriting.
  • Math: counting, place value and the four operations with hands-on materials.
  • Science and geography: experiments, map puzzles and world cultures.
  • Economics: sharing, earning and saving through a classroom store.

posts.title: Fall harvest week in our classrooms
posts.summary: Apple tasting, leaf art and pumpkin math filled a busy and colorful week.

image.alt: A child watering plants in a garden bed

posts.body:
Every October we bring the season into the classroom. This year children tasted five kinds of apples, made leaf rubbings and counted pumpkin seeds.

Learning through the senses

Montessori learning starts with the senses. Smelling, touching and sorting real fall items helps children build words and early math skills.

  • Toddlers sorted leaves by color and size.
  • Preschool children weighed and measured pumpkins.
  • Kindergarten wrote short stories about the seasons.

Thank you to all the families who sent in apples and gourds!

posts.title: Five tips for a happy first day
posts.summary: Simple ways to help your child feel calm and ready for a new classroom.

image.alt: An adult reading a picture book with a young child

posts.body:
Starting school is a big step for children and parents. These small habits can make the first weeks easier.

  1. Visit together first. A short visit helps the room feel familiar.
  2. Read about school. Picture books about school start good conversations.
  3. Keep goodbyes short. A hug, a smile and a clear “see you later” work best.
  4. Bring a comfort item. A family photo or small blanket can help.
  5. Keep a routine. Regular sleep and meal times help children settle in.

Our teachers are happy to share how your child’s day went at pick-up.

posts.summary: Animals, science shows and music came to us, so children could explore without the bus.

image.alt: Children laughing on the playground swings

posts.body:
Our Summer Bridge program keeps learning fun all summer long. In July, special guests visited our schools each day.

  • A visit from friendly farm animals
  • A hands-on science show with bubbles and slime
  • A music and movement morning

In-school field trips mean more time for play and learning, and less time on the road.

posts.title: Why we use real words with toddlers
posts.summary: Toddlers can learn big words. Here is how our teachers build vocabulary every day.

image.alt: A small group reading a book together on the floor

posts.body:
In our toddler rooms, teachers use real names for things instead of baby talk. A “dog” is a dog, and a “digger” is an excavator.

Why it matters

Young children soak up language. When they hear rich, clear words, their vocabulary grows quickly and they learn to express their needs.

Try it at home

  • Name what you see on walks and at the store.
  • Read a book together every day.
  • Give your child time to answer before you help.

posts.title: Eight years of Readers’ Choice Awards
posts.summary: Looking back on eight years of awards voted by local families.

image.alt: A family running and laughing together in the park

posts.body:
We are proud to have won the Readers’ Choice Award every year from 2017 to 2024. This award comes from the votes of local families, so it means a lot to our teachers.

Thank you to every parent who voted, shared a review or told a friend about us. We look forward to many more years of learning together.
